scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Koftos is a traditional Greek folk dance typical of Thessaly, Epirus, and central Greece.
The word 'Koftos' in Greek means 'to cut', referring to the periodic interruptions built into the music and tune.
It acts as a faster version of the traditional Syrtos.
on_screen: Map: Greece · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Koftos is a lively social dance.
Its name and character are defined by the abrupt breaks in the music, which create a playful tension between the musicians and the dancers.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danced in a two-measure (sta dio) style, Koftos is a faster Syrtos.
Dancers move in a line or circle and can also move backwards, forwards, or dance with partners.
When the music suddenly stops, dancers freeze or execute sharp accent gestures—shouting 'Hey!', clapping, or moving their arms up or down.
Watch for The Cut (Koftos Stop).
